questions.stem: An electron micrograph of a liver cell shows organelles with a double membrane, the inner membrane being highly folded. Which organelle is being observed, and what is the purpose of the folds?

options.text: Chloroplast — the folds increase light absorption
Nucleus — the folds store genetic material
Mitochondrion — the inner folds (cristae) increase the surface area for aerobic respiration reactions
Ribosome — the folds allow protein synthesis to occur

questions.explanation: Mitochondria have a distinctive double membrane structure. The inner membrane is folded into cristae, which greatly increase the surface area available for the reactions of aerobic respiration, allowing more ATP to be produced.

questions.stem: A scientist compares cells from heart muscle and skin tissue under an electron microscope. She observes that heart muscle cells contain significantly more mitochondria. What is the best explanation?

options.text: Heart cells need more mitochondria to store oxygen
Heart cells contract continuously and require a much greater supply of ATP from aerobic respiration
Skin cells do not carry out respiration
Heart cells are larger, so they need more mitochondria to fill the space

questions.explanation: The heart beats continuously, so cardiac muscle cells have extremely high energy demands. More mitochondria means more aerobic respiration can occur, producing the ATP needed for constant contraction. All living cells respire, but some need more energy than others.

questions.stem: The matrix of a mitochondrion contains enzymes and its own DNA. A student asks why mitochondria have their own DNA. Which is the most scientifically accepted explanation?

options.text: Mitochondrial DNA controls the cell cycle
Mitochondria were once independent prokaryotic organisms that were engulfed by ancestral cells (endosymbiotic theory)
Mitochondrial DNA is a backup copy of nuclear DNA
The DNA is needed to break down glucose in the cytoplasm

questions.explanation: The endosymbiotic theory proposes that mitochondria were once free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by larger cells. Evidence for this includes their own DNA, double membrane, and ability to replicate independently — similar features to bacteria.

questions.stem: A drug is discovered that causes the cristae of mitochondria to unfold and become smooth. What effect would this have on a cell's ability to produce ATP?

options.text: ATP production would increase because the membrane is now more permeable
ATP production would decrease because the surface area for respiratory reactions is reduced
ATP production would be unaffected because ATP is made in the cytoplasm
ATP production would stop completely because the outer membrane is damaged

questions.explanation: The cristae provide a large surface area for the enzymes and proteins involved in the later stages of aerobic respiration. If the cristae unfold, the surface area decreases dramatically, reducing the rate of ATP production. Some ATP could still be made, but at a much lower rate.

questions.stem: Sperm cells have mitochondria arranged in a spiral around the midpiece of the tail. How does this structural adaptation relate to the sperm cell's function?

options.text: The mitochondria protect the genetic material in the sperm head
The mitochondria provide ATP for the tail to move, enabling the sperm to swim towards the egg
The spiral shape helps the sperm cell divide more quickly
The mitochondria store the nutrients the sperm needs to survive

questions.explanation: Sperm cells must swim long distances to reach the egg, which requires a lot of energy. The mitochondria packed into the midpiece carry out aerobic respiration to produce the ATP needed to power the tail's movement (flagellum).
